content.text:
The text combines an 1866–1880 diary with nineteenth-century scientific, industrial, agricultural, and social articles. The diarist records weddings, family deaths, Dickens’s lecture, travel from New York to England, London, Scotland, the Isle of Wight, Paris, and return home. She describes Spurgeon, Grant, Cuyler, American politics, and family life, ending her journal after Anna’s 1880 marriage to California.  

Other selections discuss Descartes’s circulation theory, animal souls, scientific method, and practical philosophy; naval medical service at Haslar Hospital, voyages through Madeira and Saint Helena, African anti-slavery patrols, Lamoo, and life aboard gunboats; gas burettes, engines, furnaces, fans, coke breakers, printing machinery, and bone-charcoal regeneration; soap, cottonseed oil, nutrition, scurvy, snake poison, fingerprints, lucidity, fire-resistant apparatus, building stones, farming, lime kilns, apple jelly, grape bags, solar heat, and determining the true meridian.
